description: rangeStrategy: always bump dependencies, even when the new version is already in the range.
rebaseWhen: rebase only on conflicts, to save unnecessary workflow runs.

gitIgnoredAuthors: the workflows that commit to Renovate branches (Automated npm dedupe for Renovate, Binaries Lock Check) commit as github-actions. Without this, Renovate would see the branch as modified by someone else and stop rebasing and updating it.
internalChecksFilter: hold updates that do not yet satisfy minimumReleaseAge instead of raising a pending PR, which would run CI and fail pnpm's minimumReleaseAge policy.
ignoreDeps: node must be the version bundled in Electron; ubuntu must be the oldest possible version, for binary compatibility with older operating systems.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Security fixes must not be delayed by minimumReleaseAge.

group.description: A group is titled like a single update, "Update dependency <group> to <version>", rather than "Update <group> to <version>".

description: mise.lock pins a checksum and a URL per tool per platform, but a local `mise install` re-locks only the platform it runs on and silently leaves the other seven stale.
Lock file maintenance runs plain `mise lock`, which refreshes every tool on every platform already in the file.
Defaults are disabled and weekly, hence the explicit settings. The packageRules keep it to mise.lock, since pnpm-lock.yaml is maintained by its own workflows and does not want a periodic refresh PR.

packageRules.description: No lock file maintenance by default: pnpm-lock.yaml is maintained by its own workflows.
Lock file maintenance for mise.lock only.

Delay npm updates until they satisfy pnpm's minimumReleaseAge policy (1 day by default since pnpm v11). Only npm packages land in pnpm-lock.yaml, so this is scoped to the npm datasource and leaves the other datasources untouched.

description: peerDependencies are not bumped by vulnerability fixes either.

Renovate turns every vulnerability alert into a package rule appended after these ones, with the vulnerabilityAlerts settings in its force object. Forced settings override every other rule, so vulnerabilityAlerts.rangeStrategy replaces the widen strategy above, and no package rule can put it back.

Package rules are applied again to each update after the lookup, when the update already carries isVulnerabilityAlert. This rule drops the peer range change from the fix at that point, while the other dependencies in the same fix keep the bump strategy.

packageRules.description: Patch updates only. The override of @kubernetes/client-node's @types/node follows the same rule, so that it stays on the catalog's version.
One PR for @types/node and its override for @kubernetes/client-node, which must stay on the same version.
One PR for http-proxy-3 and the override that points http-proxy at it, which are the same package and must stay on the same version.

customManagers.description: Renovate hints in a comment after the version.

GitHub-hosted runners in a build matrix, marked with a datasource=github-runners hint. The github-actions manager reads only a literal runs-on of a job, not ${{ matrix.runs-on }}. The value is split like that manager splits it (macos-15 into depName macos and version 15), with docker versioning so that a suffix such as -intel or -arm is kept. The hint carries no depName, which keeps the generic hint regex from matching the same line.
